props.title: The perceptron
props.subtitle: A linear classifier with a threshold

items: Inputs weighted, summed, passed through activation
Linear boundary — cannot solve XOR on its own
Stack perceptrons → hidden layers → non-linearity
MLP = universal function approximator (given enough width)
Sigmoid: saturates and kills gradients
Tanh: zero-centered but still saturates
ReLU: the default workhorse — cheap and sparse
GELU: smoother ReLU, popular in Transformers
Pick activation + initializer together (He for ReLU)
Forward: compute loss from inputs and current weights
Backward: ∂loss/∂w_i via recursive chain rule
Each layer has a local Jacobian — just matmul and apply
Optimizer uses gradients to update weights in place
GradientTape makes the tape explicit for debugging

props.title: Sequential vs Functional API
props.subtitle: Two Keras flavors — same training engine

items: Sequential — linear stacks, fastest to prototype
Functional — arbitrary DAGs, multi-input/multi-output
Subclass tf.keras.Model for full research flexibility
Model.summary() and plot_model() work on all three
Normalize inputs → mean 0, variance 1
Batch norm stabilizes intermediate activations
Glorot for tanh, He for ReLU — match init to activation
Bad init = vanishing or exploding gradients
